headline: Santa Ana winds from the northeast and north push temperatures into the 80s around Glendale and other LA and Ventura County valley and coastal areas on Thanksgiving and Friday, with wind advisories likely, before cooling over the weekend and a potentially strong rainstorm late next Tuesday into Wednesday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Tonight and Wednesday stay dry around Glendale and across Los Angeles County as offshore winds (blowing from inland toward the coast) begin to build; Burbank and LAX stay clear, with a 30 percent chance of a light east wind at LAX between 10 PM tonight and Thursday afternoon. Low clouds and a warmer air mass will keep tonight milder than last night in inland areas, so no frost or freeze alerts are expected. A Northern California storm just barely skims San Luis Obispo County, bringing a slight chance of light showers to the Central Coast tonight into Wednesday morning (30–50 percent around Santa Maria, San Luis Obispo and Paso Robles from about 2 AM to 7 AM), with any rain likely under a tenth of an inch.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Offshore winds peak around Thanksgiving morning, with an unusually strong push from the north as well as the northeast, which tends to send stronger northerly winds into the LA valleys, including the Glendale and Burbank areas, and less wind across western Ventura County than a typical Santa Ana. Combined with high pressure building over California, this pushes highs into the 80s on Thanksgiving and Friday in many coastal and valley areas of LA and Ventura Counties and well into the 70s on the Central Coast. At least low-end wind advisories are a good bet on both Thursday and Friday across parts of LA and Ventura Counties.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Cooling begins over the weekend, and Sunday is dry but cooler as high pressure shifts east ahead of a storm moving into the Pacific Northwest. The tail end of that storm will likely bring some light rain to Southern California Sunday night into Monday, mostly under half an inch. A second, much stronger storm is likely right behind it late next Tuesday into Wednesday, with computer models consistently showing at least a moderate and possibly strong storm: widespread rain of at least 1–2 inches and 2–5 inches on mountain slopes facing the storm over a 6–8 hour period. Neither storm is especially cold, so any snow should stay above about 8,000 feet.

coast: A large, long-period west swell peaks Wednesday and Thursday, combining with very high tides to bring significant surf and significant coastal flooding. The worst is expected on the Central Coast and Ventura County beaches, with somewhat smaller but still concerning problems elsewhere: many strong rip currents nearly everywhere, strong along-shore currents, a risk of sneaker waves, heavy shore break, beach erosion and possible breaking waves at harbor entrances. Central Coast beaches have a Coastal Flood Advisory and High Surf Advisory until 6 AM Wednesday, then a Coastal Flood Warning and High Surf Warning from 6 AM Wednesday to noon Thursday. Ventura County beaches have a Coastal Flood Advisory and High Surf Advisory until 8 AM Wednesday, then a Coastal Flood Warning and High Surf Warning from 8 AM Wednesday to noon Thursday. Malibu and Los Angeles County beaches have a Coastal Flood Advisory until 6 AM Thursday, a Coastal Flood Watch Thursday morning, and a High Surf Advisory from 10 AM Wednesday to 9 PM Thursday; the Santa Barbara south coast has a Coastal Flood Advisory until noon Thursday and a High Surf Advisory from 8 AM Wednesday to noon Thursday. For boaters, Small Craft Advisories run through 3 PM Thursday (some waters starting Wednesday or early Thursday), with seas peaking at 14–18 feet on the outer waters and 13–16 feet north of Point Sal on Wednesday. Closer in, advisory-level winds are expected in the western Santa Barbara Channel Wednesday and from Point Mugu to Santa Monica Thursday, with a 40–60 percent chance of widespread advisory-level seas Wednesday through Thursday. Friday night through Sunday brings lighter winds, though advisory-level seas may linger offshore (50–70 percent chance) and north of Point Sal (40–60 percent), and the western Santa Barbara Channel has a 50 percent chance of advisory-level winds Sunday afternoon and evening.
watch_for: Likely wind advisories Thanksgiving and Friday in parts of LA and Ventura Counties, with stronger-than-usual north winds into the LA valleys.
Coastal flood and high surf warnings Wednesday into Thursday on the Central Coast and Ventura County beaches, and a Coastal Flood Watch for LA County beaches Thursday morning.
A potentially strong storm late next Tuesday into Wednesday with 1–2 inches of rain widely and 2–5 inches on mountain slopes.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the dry, warm, windy stretch through Friday, and models have been consistent for several runs on next week's stronger storm, though its exact strength (moderate versus strong) is still uncertain.
